I currently have a dual boot with Windows on a 64GB SSD and Arch Linux on a 500GB HDD and I'm thinking of getting rid of Windows. What would be the best way to partition these drives?

I think my /home is going to be too big for the SSD because of Steam and Wine and such, and I've read you shouldn't put /var on SSD because of frequent writes. I suppose swap could also go on the HDD since I have plenty of RAM? That would leave me with /boot and / on the SSD. Is this alright or am I missing a lot of the performance benefits by leaving so much stuff on the HDD?

What about the file systems? I'm assuming /boot should still be ext2, but should I pick F2FS over ext4 for the rest of the SSD?

• I'd put swap, /var, /tmp and /home on the 500GB HD, and the rest on the SSD. Why would /boot be ext2?
  • From this SSD testing on Linux 4.0, it seems Btrfs and F2FS do indeed have some performance improvements to find with this new (4.0) kernel -- at least with solid-state storage and using the default mount options.
  • You need swap.
  • You might miss out on a bit of performance on your gaming, but SSD's tend to fail without warning, personally, I'd rather be safe than sorry.

My /boot is currently ext2, to be honest I don't remember why. Would F2FS be alright for /boot as well? EDIT: I assume not?

I think /tmp is automatically mounted as tmpfs on Arch.

It depends on if your bootloader supports it, and I don't think any of them do.

Grub doesn't list it in its supported filesystems.

If it weren't for that, you could always make sure F2FS was baked into your initrd so you could read root to boot.

But you don't have to use ext2, you can use Ext3 or 4 for /boot and that'll work.
